interest: Japanese espionage in Bombay and the 1943 propaganda push with Subhas Chandra Bose.
keywords: State Department Division of Far Eastern Affairs
overview: This file (State Department decimal 894.20245) contains records spanning October 1941 to October 1944 relating to Japanese military activities, intelligence gathering, espionage, and propaganda concerning India. Consisting of a series of cross-reference sheets and an analytical memorandum from the Division of Far Eastern Affairs, the file covers pre-Pearl Harbor consular espionage in Bombay involving commercial intelligence compiled in Los Angeles, the role of Indian nationalist figures such as Rash Behari Bose and Subhas Chandra Bose aligned with Tokyo, Premier Hideki Tojo's public pledge to support Indian independence, regional reactions in Afghanistan, propaganda operations in Bangkok involving the Ghadr Party, and British-Allied directives regarding Indian prisoners of war escaping Japanese-occupied territories.
